### prerequisites (listed separately)
1. **-> optical_ext_switch_difference_credit**, form `state`. policy_source "The accidental replacement charge is fixed only after the original base-lens charge carries the switch-down credit owed for any lower-priced lens design the job has been remade in." — carried verbatim in accidental_damage_replacement_authorization, "Conditions on fixing the charge", 1st sentence; connective "only after" and state form intact. Found in no other document (scoped grep for the phrase over `docs/*/*.json`: hits in other products' docs are their own different sentences). Resolution basis: switch_down_credit_entry "When a non-adapt remake moves an eyewear job to a lens design whose base lens price is lower than the original base-lens charge, a switch-down credit is owed ... posted as one refund credit against that original base-lens charge" + records (variant now Premium 149.99, base-lens charge 199.99, no credit). Strength: hard gate in source and KB. Depended-on documents do not carry the sentence or mention the replacement.
2. **-> optical_ext_late_rx_remake_waiver**, form `state`. policy_source "The accidental replacement charge is not fixed until each prescription-change remake charge on the job, less any waiver posted against it, stands no higher than the late prescription-change remake charge it is owed at." — verbatim, same section, 2nd sentence; "not fixed until" intact. Only in the hub. Resolution basis: late_prescription_change_remake_waiver "where the remake charge booked for that remake, less every waiver already posted against it, is higher than that charge, the difference is owed back ... posted as one waiver credit" + the calculation doc + records (remake 2 prescription_change 60.00, no waiver). Strength matches.
- `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` have no home in any document (checked: the two tool names occur only in their own hubs).

## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the docs above traces to a source rule, a variant parameter, the lifecycle or a task-tool contract. Statements that are derivations rather than restatements and were checked for entailment: "The credit is owed as a matter of the job's own records ..." (switch_down_credit_entry) — follows from the rule; "A vision plan frame allowance ... is not a frame return refund" (frame_return_to_stock_refund) — follows from the credit reasons; "Eyewear is never shipped" FAQ — base rule.
- Added steps / confirmations / reviews / notifications: none found (no "confirm with the member", no "review", no "notify").
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none — no "if unmet, first call <tool>"; each of the 7 task tools is named only in its own hub (scoped grep of the tool suffixes over `docs/*/*.json`).
- Task opening world state written as policy fact: none; every example is marked hypothetical. Some hypothetical figures are price-list combinations that also occur in seeded jobs (e.g. Premium + polycarbonate upgrade 30.00), derived from the schedules, not from records — not world state.
- Omissions / rewrites: none at the level of entailment. Observation (not a defect): the "otherwise" tier of several factor ladders equals the baseline value and is rendered in the factor document as "outside this schedule/card/table" or "sets no ..." rather than as a figure; the computation document supplies the figure, which is exactly how the source rule sentences themselves are worded ("... instead of ..."), so the ladder is entailed in full.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No KB-BIJECTION RED. First revision; no prior revisions.

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts):
- The accidental baseline rule itself says "The replacement percentage is set from the whole months between the replacement clock start and the day the replacement is authorized" while fixing the baseline percentage at 30 percent; the months only bear on the factor ladder. The KB carries this sentence as the source has it.
- Retiring "Any other remake, or one past its window or count, costs remake_charge_pct_outside_coverage ..." leaves remakes other than late prescription-change remakes (e.g. a non-adapt remake past its window) with no priced rule in force; the KB faithfully writes the clause as retired.
- `rx_change_remakes_allowed` ("free prescription-change remakes per job") survives in parameter_schema although the clause that used it is retired; adaptation_and_prescription_change_guarantees renders the parameter meaning faithfully.
